title: Start a jacket's separating zip: seat the pin fully in the box, then zip it up
context: Garment finishers check every jacket's zip before bagging, and outdoor-gear repairers start the same separating (open-ended) zips on tents and coats. The trade rule: hold the retainer box steady, push the insertion pin all the way down into the box, then pull the slider. A pin left a few mm short sets every right tooth out of step with its left mate, so the slider climbs the left half alone and the zip splits behind it; it has to go back down to start again. Here the pin starts 5 mm short, and its snug push shoves the loose jacket front away unless the hem is held. Unlike #20 (push one loose plug home), nothing looks wrong until the zip is run, and the second hand must hold the base. Unlike #707 (hold a case lid shut while zipping), the closure fails silently from a short pin rather than jamming. Unlike #1247 (seat buds before a lid), the short part lets the closure run and splits it. Done by: hand sewers; inspectors, testers and sorters (O*NET 51-6051.00, 51-9061.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Parts are a separating zip scaled 2.5x. Jacket left front (navy polyester shell, 35 g, loose on the table): a 0.2 cm panel from x 14.6 to 39.6, y 0.7 to 22.5, a 1 cm tall hem band along its near edge (x 13 to 14.6), the black acetal retainer box (1.8 x 1.85 x 0.8 cm) at x 14.6 to 16.4 by the zip line (y 0), and the left tooth row (0.7 cm wide, 0.45 cm tall, acetal) up to a top stop at x 39. Zinc-alloy slider (12 g) parked on the box, x 16.4 to 20.2, with an upright pull (2.6 x 1.2 x 1 cm). Right half: black acetal insertion pin (6 g) in the slider's right channel, its bottom end 5 mm short of home, with an orange grip tab (1.4 x 1.3 x 1.4 cm) on its stiffened tape end at x 21.2 to 22.6 (seated), y -5 to -3.7, beside the tape; then six 2 cm tape sections (4 g each, 3 cm navy tape plus a tooth row) on joints that let the tape curl away from the left half by 5 deg each.
scoring: From the poses of the jacket front, pin, slider and tape sections (on a real rig: the pin's gap at the box, the slider's height, and whether each right tooth group sits interlocked beside its left mates). A tape section interlocks as the slider's bottom edge clears its top by 1 to 12 mm, if it lies within 1.2 mm of its zipped place along the zip (2.5 mm across, 6 deg); the slider back below a section opens it. Pin home: within 0.8 mm of the bottom of the box. Split: the slider above a section that did not interlock. Score: 0 while split; otherwise 0.25 for the pin home, 0.5 with at least 3 of 6 sections interlocked, 1.0 with all 6 (zipped to the top stop). Halved unless both grippers are 2.5 cm clear of every part and everything is still. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the slider back down onto the box (this unzips it), draw the pin 5 mm back out of the box and let the right tape lie loose beside the left half; put the jacket front back square on its marks.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), parts 2.5x. The left front is one free rigid body (panel, hem band, box, tooth row); the right tape is six rigid 2 cm sections on sprung hinges. Pin and slider ride joints with 1.2 N and 0.3 N friction; the slider's flange herds the tape by contact. Interlock rule: as the slider clears a section lying within 1.2 mm of its zipped place, the task welds it there; sliding back down frees it. No cloth or tooth contact; scored from poses.
